state.name: New Jersey
state.agency: New Jersey Division of Fish and Wildlife (NJ Fish & Wildlife), New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection
state.peak_intrusion_season: February through April during raccoon and squirrel denning, spring for groundhog and skunk emergence, summer for bat maternity colonies (exclusion only inside the NJ Fish & Wildlife guideline windows), and late September through November as squirrels and rodents seek winter shelter
state.climate_factor: New Jersey's humid summers and cold winters push squirrels, raccoons and rodents into attics hard each fall, while the Shore's empty off-season homes let bat and raccoon problems grow undetected for months
state.permit_note: New Jersey has no nuisance wildlife control operator license: under the Game Code, N.J.A.C. 7:25-5.21, control of squirrel, raccoon, opossum, skunk, woodchuck and fox causing property damage is done by the property owner or their agent designated in writing, and species outside that list require a NJ Fish & Wildlife depredation permit; the separate NJDEP Commercial Pesticide Applicator license (Category 7A) covers pesticide and rodenticide application for hire and is not a wildlife license

Atlantic County.region: southern New Jersey on the Atlantic coast, between the Pine Barrens and the Shore
Atlantic County.nearest_metro: Atlantic City is itself the regional center, with Philadelphia about 60 miles northwest
natural_features: Edwin B. Forsythe National Wildlife Refuge
Great Egg Harbor River
Wharton State Forest edge and the Pine Barrens
Atlantic County.habitat_type: casino and Shore housing in the east, Pine Barrens forest and blueberry and cranberry farms inland
Atlantic County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats turn up constantly in Shore homes that sit closed between rentals, skunks work the sandy back-bay neighborhoods, and Pine Barrens-edge properties in Galloway and Hammonton see snakes and groundhogs along the tree line
Atlantic County.absent_or_rare: black bears are uncommon visitors this far south, and beaver, deer and wild turkey problems in the Barrens are NJ Fish & Wildlife matters rather than a routine house call

Bergen County.region: northeastern New Jersey across the Hudson from New York City
Bergen County.nearest_metro: New York City (Fort Lee sits at the George Washington Bridge)
natural_features: Overpeck County Park and the Hackensack River
Ramapo Mountains foothills in the northwest
Palisades Interstate Park along the Hudson
Bergen County.habitat_type: dense older suburbs and apartment towns in the south and east, wooded large-lot towns toward the Ramapo foothills
Bergen County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats run the older commercial and multifamily blocks of Hackensack, Englewood and Fort Lee, raccoons and squirrels are relentless in the mature-canopy suburbs of Ridgewood and Teaneck, and groundhogs burrow the Ramapo-edge yards in the northwest towns
Bergen County.absent_or_rare: venomous snakes are not a Bergen County pattern — the county's rocky northwest is copperhead country only at its far edge, and black bear sightings are handled by NJ Fish & Wildlife

Burlington County.region: central-southern New Jersey, the state's largest county by area, from the Delaware River to the Pine Barrens
Burlington County.nearest_metro: Philadelphia (about 20 miles west across the Delaware River)
natural_features: Wharton State Forest
Rancocas State Park and Rancocas Creek
Brendan T. Byrne State Forest
Burlington County.habitat_type: Delaware River towns in the west, established suburbs in the northwest, and deep Pine Barrens forest across the eastern half
Burlington County.regional_wildlife: the suburban northwest — Moorestown, Marlton and Mount Laurel side streets — produces steady squirrel, raccoon and mole work, while the Barrens towns around Medford and Tabernacle add groundhogs, snakes in the pines, and bats in older farmhouses and lake cabins
Burlington County.absent_or_rare: the Pine Barrens' southern timber rattlesnake population lives in the deep forest townships, a state-Endangered species that is referral-only through NJ Fish & Wildlife, and beaver flooding in the Barrens is a permit matter

Camden County.region: southwestern New Jersey across the Delaware River from Philadelphia
natural_features: Cooper River Park and the Cooper River
Newton Lake and the Cooper River corridor
Wharton State Forest edge in Winslow
Camden County.habitat_type: dense older city and inner-suburb blocks in the north, postwar suburbs in the center, and Pine Barrens forest in the southeast
Camden County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats are entrenched in Camden City's older blocks and the Pennsauken industrial edges, raccoons and squirrels fill Cherry Hill and Haddonfield attics under heavy canopy, and Winslow's Barrens-edge homes add groundhogs and the occasional pine snake sighting
Camden County.absent_or_rare: there are no venomous snakes established in Camden County's suburbs, and deer and beaver problems along the Cooper River are NJ Fish & Wildlife matters

Cape May County.region: the southern tip of New Jersey, a peninsula between Delaware Bay and the Atlantic Ocean
Cape May County.nearest_metro: Atlantic City (about 35 miles northeast) and Philadelphia (about 80 miles northwest)
natural_features: Cape May Point State Park
Delaware Bayshore marshes
Belleplain State Forest
Cape May County.habitat_type: barrier-island beach towns, bayshore villages, and a wooded mainland spine
Cape May County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, skunks and bats are the standing problem in beach houses and rentals that sit empty for weeks in Ocean City, Wildwood and Cape May, and mainland towns around Cape May Court House and Belleplain add squirrels and groundhogs at the forest edge
Cape May County.absent_or_rare: Cape May County has no established venomous snakes, and the county's famous bird migrations and osprey nests on structures are protected — deterrence and timing work, not removal

Cumberland County.region: southwestern New Jersey along Delaware Bay, the state's farm belt
Cumberland County.nearest_metro: Philadelphia (about 45 miles northeast) and Wilmington, Delaware (about 35 miles northwest)
natural_features: Maurice River and its tidal marshes
Union Lake
Parvin State Park edge and the bayshore wetlands
Cumberland County.habitat_type: flat farmland, small older cities, and Delaware Bay marsh and fishing villages
Cumberland County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs work the farm edges and outbuildings that define Cumberland County, rats follow the older commercial blocks and food businesses in Bridgeton, Vineland and Millville, and raccoons and bats settle the bayshore villages around Port Norris and Mauricetown
Cumberland County.absent_or_rare: venomous snakes are not established in Cumberland County, and muskrat and beaver work in the Maurice River marshes is a NJ Fish & Wildlife permit matter

Essex County.region: northeastern New Jersey, home to Newark and the first ring of New York suburbs
Essex County.nearest_metro: Newark is itself a metro center, with New York City about 10 miles east
natural_features: Branch Brook Park
Eagle Rock Reservation
South Mountain Reservation edge
Essex County.habitat_type: dense urban core in the east rising to wooded Watchung ridges in the west
Essex County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats are the dominant call in Newark, East Orange and Irvington, where older multifamily blocks, alleys and sewers sit wall to wall, while the Watchung towns — Montclair, West Orange, Livingston — produce raccoon, squirrel and bat work in large older homes under heavy canopy
Essex County.absent_or_rare: Essex County has no venomous snakes, and its park deer and Canada goose problems are municipal and NJ Fish & Wildlife matters, not house calls

Gloucester County.region: southwestern New Jersey across from Philadelphia, between the suburbs and the farm belt
Gloucester County.nearest_metro: Philadelphia (about 15 miles northwest across the Delaware River)
natural_features: Tall Pines State Preserve
Scotland Run Park
Delaware River waterfront at West Deptford
Gloucester County.habitat_type: fast-growing suburbs in the north, college-town Glassboro, and farmland and orchards in the south
Gloucester County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow under sheds and decks across the farm-edge subdivisions of Washington Township, Monroe and Harrison, squirrels and raccoons fill attics in Deptford and Woodbury's older stock, and moles work the big new-subdivision lawns in Mantua and Woolwich
Gloucester County.absent_or_rare: venomous snakes are not established in Gloucester County, and beaver flooding on the county's creeks is a NJ Fish & Wildlife permit matter

Hudson County.region: northeastern New Jersey on the Hudson River waterfront, the most densely populated county in the state
Hudson County.nearest_metro: New York City (directly across the Hudson River)
natural_features: Liberty State Park
Hackensack Meadowlands at Secaucus
Hudson River waterfront and the Palisades
Hudson County.habitat_type: wall-to-wall urban blocks, high-rises and brownstones, with Meadowlands marsh at the western edge
Hudson County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats are the defining Hudson County call — older sewers, restaurant rows and shared-wall buildings in Jersey City, Hoboken, Union City and Bayonne let them travel block to block — with raccoons in chimneys and starlings and sparrows nesting in signs and vents along the commercial strips
Hudson County.absent_or_rare: Hudson County has no snakes of any consequence and no groundhog country outside its few parks; Canada geese on waterfront lawns are deterrence work only

Hunterdon County.region: western New Jersey along the Delaware River, the state's farm and estate county
Hunterdon County.nearest_metro: the Lehigh Valley and New York metro fringe (New York City about 60 miles east)
natural_features: Spruce Run Recreation Area
Round Valley Reservoir
South Branch of the Raritan River and the Hunterdon plateau
Hunterdon County.habitat_type: rolling farmland, river towns, and wooded estate country
Hunterdon County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs under barns and shed foundations are the everyday Hunterdon call, bats colonize the attics of Flemington, Clinton and Lambertville's older homes every summer, and the Sourland and Cushetunk edges add black rat snakes in barns and the isolated copperhead colonies the county is known for
Hunterdon County.absent_or_rare: timber rattlesnakes are not a Hunterdon County animal — the county's venomous snake is the copperhead, state-Threatened and referral-only — and bear and beaver problems belong to NJ Fish & Wildlife

Mercer County.region: central New Jersey, home to Trenton and Princeton, between the Delaware River and the Sourlands
Mercer County.nearest_metro: Trenton and Princeton anchor the county, with Philadelphia about 35 miles southwest
natural_features: Delaware and Raritan Canal State Park
Mercer Meadows and the Lawrence-Hopewell trail country
Sourland Mountain Preserve edge
Mercer County.habitat_type: state-capital city, university town, and established suburbs between river and ridge
Mercer County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold Trenton's older rowhouses and commercial blocks, raccoons and squirrels work the big-canopy neighborhoods of Princeton and Lawrence, and the Sourland edge in Hopewell adds copperhead sightings — state-Threatened, look-don't-touch — alongside groundhogs and bats in farmhouses
Mercer County.absent_or_rare: the Sourlands hold one of the isolated copperhead populations named in state guidance; timber rattlesnakes do not occur in Mercer County, and canal-corridor beaver work is a permit matter

Middlesex County.region: central New Jersey along the Raritan River, the state's crossroads county
Middlesex County.nearest_metro: New Brunswick is a regional center, with New York City about 35 miles northeast
natural_features: Raritan River and the Raritan Bayshore
Cheesequake State Park
Delaware and Raritan Canal corridor
Middlesex County.habitat_type: dense older cities, warehouse corridors, and large postwar suburbs
Middlesex County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats follow the older housing and food corridors of New Brunswick, Perth Amboy and the Route 1 and 9 strips, raccoons and squirrels are constant in Edison, Woodbridge and East Brunswick's canopy suburbs, and Cheesequake-edge homes add skunks, opossums and marsh-side raccoons
Middlesex County.absent_or_rare: Middlesex County has no venomous snakes, and its bayshore muskrat and Canada goose pressure is deterrence and permit work rather than a house call

Monmouth County.region: central New Jersey on the northern Shore, between New York commuter country and the beach towns
Monmouth County.nearest_metro: New York City (about 50 miles north, with ferry and rail commuter links)
natural_features: Sandy Hook and Gateway National Recreation Area
Manasquan Reservoir
Turkey Swamp Park and the northern Pine Barrens edge
Monmouth County.habitat_type: Shore towns in the east, commuter suburbs in the center, and farm and forest in the west
Monmouth County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are the standing call in Shore homes in Long Branch, Asbury Park and the Middletown bayside that sit quiet between seasons, squirrels and moles work the Howell and Manalapan subdivisions, and Freehold-area farms add groundhogs and barn bats
Monmouth County.absent_or_rare: Monmouth County has no established venomous snakes, and osprey nests on chimneys and platforms are protected — timing and deterrence work coordinated with NJ Fish & Wildlife

Morris County.region: northern New Jersey, suburban in the east and Highland and lake country in the west
natural_features: Great Swamp National Wildlife Refuge
Lake Hopatcong
Black River and the Morris Highlands
Morris County.habitat_type: established eastern suburbs, lake communities, and forested Highlands ridges
Morris County.regional_wildlife: bats are a signature Morris County job — the county's two abandoned mine complexes are the state's documented bat hibernation sites, and older homes in Morristown, Madison and Chatham host summer colonies — while lake homes on Hopatcong add raccoons and squirrels, and the Highlands add black snakes and the occasional copperhead report
Morris County.absent_or_rare: timber rattlesnakes live along the northern Highlands ridges, state-Endangered and referral-only through the Venomous Snake Response Team, and Great Swamp beaver and deer work belongs to NJ Fish & Wildlife

Ocean County.region: central New Jersey Shore, the state's fastest-growing retirement and beach county
Ocean County.nearest_metro: the northern Shore commuter belt, with New York City about 70 miles north
natural_features: Barnegat Bay and Island Beach State Park
Double Trouble State Park and the Pine Barrens
Cattus Island County Park
Ocean County.habitat_type: barrier-island and lagoon communities in the east, fast-growing suburbs in the center, Pine Barrens in the west
Ocean County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, skunks and bats move into lagoon and beach homes in Brick, Berkeley and Barnegat that sit empty between visits, Lakewood and Jackson's wooded subdivisions produce heavy squirrel and raccoon volume, and the Barrens edge adds groundhogs and pine snakes in the western townships
Ocean County.absent_or_rare: the Pine Barrens timber rattlesnake population reaches Ocean County's deep forest — state-Endangered, referral-only — and northern pine snakes here are state-Threatened and never handled

Passaic County.region: northeastern New Jersey, split between the Paterson urban corridor and the Highlands lake country
natural_features: Great Falls National Historical Park and the Passaic River
Greenwood Lake and the Wanaque Reservoir country
Ramapo Mountain State Forest edge
Passaic County.habitat_type: dense older cities in the south, suburbs in the center, and forested reservoir and lake country in the north
Passaic County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats run Paterson, Passaic and Clifton's older multifamily and commercial blocks, raccoons and squirrels work Wayne's canopy suburbs, and West Milford and Ringwood lake homes add bats, raccoons and black snakes around the reservoirs
Passaic County.absent_or_rare: copperheads occur in the county's rocky northern woods but are uncommon and state-Threatened — identification and referral, never a removal promise — and reservoir watershed wildlife is managed with NJ Fish & Wildlife

Salem County.region: southwestern New Jersey on Delaware Bay, the state's most rural county
Salem County.nearest_metro: Wilmington, Delaware (about 15 miles west across the Delaware River)
natural_features: Salem River and the Delaware Bayshore marshes
Parvin State Park
Alloway Creek and Mannington marshes
Salem County.habitat_type: flat farmland, bayshore marsh, and small historic towns
Salem County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and raccoons around barns, grain storage and farmhouses are the everyday Salem County call, bats roost in Salem City and Woodstown's older homes, and rats concentrate in the older riverfront blocks of Salem and Pennsville
Salem County.absent_or_rare: Salem County has no venomous snakes, and its marsh muskrat and beaver work is a NJ Fish & Wildlife permit matter rather than a house call

Somerset County.region: central New Jersey between the Watchung ridges and the Sourlands
Somerset County.nearest_metro: the central New Jersey corporate corridor, with New York City about 45 miles northeast
natural_features: Great Swamp National Wildlife Refuge edge
Sourland Mountain Preserve
Raritan River and the Delaware and Raritan Canal
Somerset County.habitat_type: corporate-corridor suburbs, Watchung ridge towns, and Sourland farm country
Somerset County.regional_wildlife: squirrels, raccoons and moles are steady across Bridgewater, Hillsborough and Franklin's subdivision lawns and canopy streets, Great Swamp-edge towns add bats in older homes, and the Sourlands add groundhogs, black snakes and the county's isolated copperhead colonies
Somerset County.absent_or_rare: copperheads in the Sourlands are state-Threatened and referral-only, timber rattlesnakes do not occur in Somerset County, and Great Swamp wildlife is a federal refuge matter

Sussex County.region: northwestern New Jersey, the state's Skylands — Kittatinny Ridge, lakes and farms
Sussex County.nearest_metro: the New York metro exurban fringe (New York City about 65 miles east)
natural_features: Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area
Kittatinny Ridge and Stokes State Forest
Lake Mohawk and the county's glacial lakes
Sussex County.habitat_type: mountain ridge, lake communities, and dairy farm valleys
Sussex County.regional_wildlife: bats and raccoons in lake homes around Mohawk, Hopatcong and Culver are the summer staple, groundhogs work the farm valleys around Newton and Wantage, and the Kittatinny Ridge holds the state's best-known timber rattlesnake country — state-Endangered, strictly referral
Sussex County.absent_or_rare: the northern copperhead is also present along the ridge and is state-Threatened; black bears are Sussex County's signature animal and every bear problem goes to NJ Fish & Wildlife, not a house call

Union County.region: northeastern New Jersey, dense first-ring suburbs west of Staten Island
Union County.nearest_metro: New York City (about 15 miles east, across Staten Island)
natural_features: Warinanco Park and the Elizabeth River
Watchung Reservation
Arthur Kill waterfront
Union County.habitat_type: dense older suburbs and small cities under heavy street canopy
Union County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats follow the older multifamily and commercial blocks of Elizabeth, Linden and Rahway, raccoons and squirrels are constant in Westfield, Cranford and Union's canopy suburbs, and Watchung Reservation-edge homes add skunks, opossums and groundhogs
Union County.absent_or_rare: Union County has no venomous snakes, and Arthur Kill marsh wildlife and goose problems are deterrence and permit matters

Warren County.region: western New Jersey along the Delaware River, between the Kittatinny Ridge and the farm valleys
Warren County.nearest_metro: the Lehigh Valley (Easton and Allentown, Pennsylvania, directly across the Delaware River)
natural_features: Delaware River and the Delaware Water Gap southern reach
Jenny Jump State Forest
Pequest River and trout-stream valleys
Warren County.habitat_type: river towns, farm valleys, and forested ridge country
Warren County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs under barns and outbuildings lead in the farm valleys around Hope, Blairstown and Allamuchy, bats settle older homes in Belvidere, Washington and Hackettstown, and the Jenny Jump and Kittatinny edges add black snakes and rattlesnake country at the county's northern tip
Warren County.absent_or_rare: timber rattlesnakes along the northern ridge are state-Endangered and referral-only through the Venomous Snake Response Team, and Warren County black bear problems go to NJ Fish & Wildlife
